novelty.area: Verifier/critic-based LLM answer selection and aggregation (self-verification, CoVe, GenRM, LLM-as-judge reranking, debate, best-of-N with verifiers, verifier-weighted voting, selective/deliberative verification)
novelty.verdict: Blunt scorecard. Claim (i) — IV framing with necessity/sufficiency theorems: NOVEL FRAMING, STANDARD MATHEMATICS. No paper in the verifier/critic aggregation literature frames verification prompts as instruments for identification (my searches for IV framing in verifier aggregation came up empty). But the theorem CONTENT is largely published: Theorem 1 is the classical label-switching/sign non-identifiability of latent-truth models (Dawid–Skene 1979 tradition; weak-supervision theory recovers accuracies 'up to sign'; arXiv:2510.23874 proves strict identifiability for LLM raters by explicitly imposing error-rate < 0.5 to break exactly this ambiguity). Theorem 2 is a Mann–Whitney tail bound. And ISC's own Corollary admits the anchor is just the better-than-chance assumption relocated onto a designed channel — which is how Dawid–Skene-style models have always broken the symmetry. Narrow (i) to: 'the anchored-instrument framing of PROMPT DESIGN for per-item world identification, with the necessity result for arbitrarily many unanchored channels' — and cite 2510.23874 and the weak-supervision sign-ambiguity literature or a referee will. Claim (ii) — instrument queries identify the SIGNED reliability of a separate confidence channel, label-free, rather than rescoring answers: OPEN; nothing found does this. Weaver (arXiv:2506.18203) is the nearest miss and must be engaged head-on: it estimates channel reliabilities label-free via weak supervision, but the channels are the verifiers themselves and the output is per-item rescoring; no one uses a designed verifier channel to decide the world and then measures the self-confidence channel against instrument-anchored pseudo-labels. This is the defensible core. Claim (iii) — vanishing amortized identification tax: NOT PUBLISHED AS STATED, BUT SHALLOW. I found no theorem in this literature that per-item verifier cost → 0 at fixed precision of a shared parameter (Weaver pays verifiers on every query and amortizes by distilling into a 400M cross-encoder; selective-verification work — Verify when Uncertain, SeVRA, Adaptive Generate-Rank-Verify, AVA — reduces but never vanishes per-item cost, with no identification framing). However the result is an immediate corollary of 'shared parameter estimated on an O(1/SE²) subsample,' which weak-supervision sample-complexity results already imply; claim it as a positioning observation distinguishing ISC from rescoring methods, not as a deep theorem. Also: Phase A's margin-first instrumentation targeting is prior art in spirit (uncertainty-gated verification), and PROVE (arXiv:2410.12608) already deploys a sign-anchored-by-construction channel (program execution) inside self-consistency, label-free — so instrument constructions per se are not new; only their USE for channel identification is.
closest: Weaver: Shrinking the Generation-Verification Gap with Weak Verifiers (Saad-Falcon et al., 2025): The single biggest threat. It already does 'estimate channel reliabilities label-free over an unlabeled corpus, then use them as aggregation weights.' Differences that keep ISC alive: (1) the reliabilities estimated are those of the VERIFIER channels themselves, used to rescore/rank answers per item — not to identify the sign of a separate self-confidence channel; (2) Weaver is empirical, inheriting but not proving identifiability theory; (3) verifiers run on every query (cost reduced by distillation, not by a vanishing identification tax). Any ISC writeup MUST position against Weaver explicitly.

From Stochasticity to Signal: A Bayesian Latent State Model for Reliable Measurement with LLMs (2025): Directly kills the reading of claim (i) that says 'nobody proves identification theorems for label-free LLM aggregation.' ISC Theorem 1 is the classical label-switching non-identifiability of two-component mixtures restated; this paper (and Dawid–Skene / FlyingSquid-style weak-supervision theory that recovers accuracies 'up to sign' and resolves it by assumption) already contains that content. What it does NOT do: construct a sign-anchored instrument channel by prompt design, or apply it to per-item answer selection with a separate confidence channel.

Self-Verification (Weng et al., EMNLP Findings 2023) and Chain-of-Verification (Dhuliawala et al., 2023): ISC's instrument construction V_ver in §3 IS this mechanism, verbatim. Prior art for the channel itself; used purely to rescore/select per item, with no identification framing, no theorems, no amortization. ISC's spec already concedes this correctly.

Not All Votes Count! Programs as Verifiers Improve Self-Consistency (PROVE, 2024): An anchored-by-construction channel (code execution — sign fixed by mechanism, exactly ISC's ε→0 example) combined with SC voting, label-free. Kills any claim that 'sign-positive-by-construction channels inside self-consistency' are new. Still per-item filtering: no channel-reliability identification, no theorems, no amortization.

Multi-Agent Verification: Scaling Test-Time Compute with Multiple Verifiers (BoN-MAV, 2025): Multi-channel verifier aggregation for answer selection, but unweighted, per-item, no reliability estimation, no theory. Relevant baseline, not a kill.

Generative Verifiers / GenRM (Zhang et al., ICLR 2025), Cobbe et al. 2021, DiVeRSe (Li et al., 2023): Establishes verifier-weighted voting as standard; all pay verifier cost per item and need labeled training data. No identification, no sign analysis, no amortization theorem. ISC's §7 characterization of this line as 'rescoring' is accurate.

Doubly-Efficient Debate (Brown-Cohen & Irving et al., 2023) + AI Safety via Debate (Irving et al., 2018): 'Theorems about verification' exist, but they are complexity-theoretic protocol guarantees per item, not statistical identification of a confidence channel's signed coupling over a corpus. Different theorem type; cite to disambiguate, not a kill.

Selective/budget-aware verification: Verify when Uncertain (OpenReview 6tlLISSgiu); SeVRA — Think Again or Think Longer? (arXiv:2606.19808); Adaptive Generate-Rank-Verify (arXiv:2605.17609); Anytime Verified Agents (OpenReview JMDCMf7mlF): Kills the engineering novelty of ISC Phase A's 'instrument lowest-margin items first' selection rule — uncertainty-gated verification is established. None of these identify a shared channel parameter, none prove anything, and per-item verifier cost is reduced but does not vanish; no amortization result.

Label-free LLM-judge reliability estimation: CARE (arXiv:2603.00039); Calibrate, Don't Curate (arXiv:2605.09702); Judge-Aware Ranking without Ground Truth (arXiv:2601.21817); Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes (arXiv:2605.29800): Shows 'estimate verifier/judge reliability label-free' is well-trodden machinery, and the correlated-error failure mode ISC calls ε (instrument shares the model's systematic error) is empirically documented. Objective differs (evaluation metrics/model ranking, not per-item answer identification), sign resolved by assumption not construction.

novelty.area: Identification / instrumental-variable-style reasoning applied to LLMs and to weak supervision / crowdsourcing: IV and measurement-error identification, weak-supervision label-model identifiability (Snorkel / MeTaL / FlyingSquid / Firebolt), unsupervised ensemble accuracy estimation (SML, Jaffe-Nadler), anchor-based latent-class identification (anchor words, anchor points, "good-enough annotator"), Hui-Walter no-gold-standard designs, and prompt/query design as a source of identifying variation.
novelty.verdict:
Blunt: claim (i) is dead as written, claim (iii) is not a result at all, claim (ii) survives only in a narrow form. Rewrite section 7 before anyone else reads it.

(i) "Framing prompt selection as instrumental design for identification, with necessity/sufficiency theorems" — PUBLISHED, twice over, and partly WRONG.
  - The framing: Chen, Rambachan & Tamer, "Partial Identification from LLM Prompts" (arXiv:2606.15031, June 2026) is prompt/replication design as the determinant of identifying content, in a two-component mixture, with a stronger non-identification result than ISC's Theorem 1 (identified set = [0,1] even under stochastic-ordering restrictions) and a formal account of what restores identification (externally validated sensitivity/specificity bounds). They do not say "instrument", they only get partial identification, and their calibration needs labels — that is the entire gap ISC has left on the framing. Separately, Espinal Maya (arXiv:2604.02403) already uses full IV language for LLM scores and enforces the exclusion restriction by prompt wording. And Messing's TEE (arXiv:2604.11581) already treats prompt variants as a budgeted design variable.
  - The theorems: Theorem 1 is the global label-switching / sign ambiguity of conditionally independent latent-class models — Allman-Matias-Rhodes 2009 ("identifiable up to label swapping"), Snorkel/MeTaL (arXiv:1810.02840), FlyingSquid (arXiv:2002.11955), Parisi et al. PNAS 2014, Jaffe et al. AISTATS 2015, and most damningly FUSE (arXiv:2604.18547, 2026) whose Assumption 2.1 is verbatim the majority-better-than-random condition that "uniquely determines the sign". Theorem 2 is the standard symmetry breaker: better-than-random, anchor word (Arora et al. 2012), anchor point (Liu & Tao 2016; Xia et al. NeurIPS 2019), "good-enough annotator" (Ibrahim et al. NeurIPS 2019), Se+Sp>1 in Hui-Walter, or the mode/median normalization in Hu & Schennach (Econometrica 2008). The MeTaL line even states ISC's exact mechanism: fix the sign of one conditionally independent source and the sign of every other element follows.
  - Worse, the NECESSITY claim is false in general. Hui & Walter (1980) identify a two-test model with no gold standard and no sign anchor, using designed heterogeneity in prevalence across populations. Liu et al. (ICML 2023, PMLR v202) catalogue anchor points, irreducibility, separability, rankability, clusterability and redundant-label/tensor conditions as mutually alternative routes to identifiability. Theorem 1 holds only inside ISC's symmetric one-parameter confidence model with a single homogeneous population and channel-wise sign flips; state it that way or a referee will kill it in one line. A red-team on ISC should specifically test whether class-imbalance or margin heterogeneity across an item stratum breaks the two-world tie without any instrument — if it does, Theorem 1 as printed is refuted by ISC's own simulator.

(ii) "Instrument-identified signed channel reliability, label-free, not just rescoring instrumented items" — LARGELY PUBLISHED, narrow survivor.
  Weaver (arXiv:2506.18203, ICML/NeurIPS 2025) estimates signed verifier reliability label-free with a weak-supervision label model and uses it to weight selection across the whole corpus, filtering below-random verifiers. FUSE (arXiv:2604.18547, 2026) does the same by method-of-moments with an explicit identifiability theorem and a batched, corpus-shared estimation mode. Both are label-free, both propagate to non-instrumented items, both in the test-time-scaling setting. What is genuinely not published: using a CONSTRUCTED, sign-by-design query to anchor the sign of the BASE model's self-reported confidence channel per item, in the regime where the better-than-random assumption that Weaver/FUSE/SML all rely on is precisely what fails (artifact echo). That is the whole remaining novelty and it is one sentence long. Also fix the terminology: the verification query is a second MEASUREMENT of the latent truth with a known-direction normalization, not an instrument in the exclusion-restriction sense — there is no treatment being shifted. Econometrics referees will call this out; Hu & Schennach is the correct citation frame and it is a normalization there, not a discovery.

(iii) "Vanishing amortized identification tax" — NOT A RESULT. A fixed-size calibration set spread over a growing corpus giving O(1/Q) per item is the definition of a fixed cost, and it is the operating principle of PPI (Angelopoulos et al., Science 2023), stratified PPI (NeurIPS 2024), DSL (Egami et al., NeurIPS 2023), and Ludwig-Mullainathan-Rambachan (NBER w33344). FUSE's batched mode and every weak-supervision label model already share parameters corpus-wide, so the "rescoring approaches must pay per item" contrast is a straw man against the actual competition. Active WeaSuL (arXiv:2104.14847) already does margin/maxKL-targeted budget spending to fix a corpus-level label model, and arXiv:2510.14913 already runs the matched-compute votes-vs-verification split for self-consistency. Drop the amortization from the novelty list; it is a cost model, not a contribution.

What is actually left, and it is worth having: the composite claim that in the artifact-echo regime — where every sign-fixing assumption in the existing literature (majority better than random, anchor points, plurality pseudo-labels) is violated by construction — a deliberately constructed sign-anchored query is the only use of marginal trace budget that helps, with the attenuation corollary delta(1-2eps) making eps (shared-error rate between solver and checker) the single declared sensitivity parameter, and label-free diagnostics I1-I3 that detect when eps>1/2 and force a fallback. That is F1 plus F3, i.e. an empirical and diagnostic contribution, not a theoretical one. Recommended rewrite of section 7: cite Chen-Rambachan-Tamer, FUSE, Weaver, MeTaL, Hui-Walter, Hu-Schennach and Allman-Matias-Rhodes up front; concede Theorems 1-2 as restatements within a specific model; claim novelty only for (a) manufacturing the anchor at inference time by query design rather than assuming it, (b) anchoring the base confidence channel rather than the verifiers, and (c) the echo-regime budget result. Also verify the FUSE details against the paper directly — my read of its Assumption 2.1 and Theorem 2.3 came from an automated extraction of arXiv:2604.18547v1, and if that assumption is stated even slightly differently it changes how hard it hits Theorem 2.
closest: Partial Identification from LLM Prompts: This is the most dangerous single paper for claim (i). It is exactly 'prompt/query design determines what is identified', published one month ago by three top econometricians, with a sharper non-identification result than ISC Theorem 1 and a formal treatment of what restores identification. Differences that ISC can still stand on: (a) they do partial identification only, never point identification; (b) their disciplining device is externally CALIBRATED accuracy bounds obtained from a validation sample with true labels — not label-free, and not a sign-only restriction; (c) they never use the words 'instrument' or 'instrumental variable'; (d) they treat prompt variants as exchangeable measurements to aggregate over, not as a deliberately constructed sign-anchored channel; (e) corpus-level prevalence, not per-item answer selection; (f) no budget/amortization analysis. ISC must cite this and reposition Theorem 1 as a special case of their Proposition 1.

FUSE: Ensembling Verifiers with Zero Labeled Data: Kills the framing of ISC Theorems 1-2 as new: FUSE states the identifiability theorem AND names the sign assumption as the thing that resolves the ambiguity, in exactly the LLM test-time-verification setting ISC targets, four months ago. It also substantially anticipates claim (ii) (label-free signed verifier reliability) and the mechanics behind claim (iii) (corpus-shared parameters via batched estimation). What FUSE does NOT do: construct an anchor channel by designing a new query; it assumes the majority-better-than-random condition rather than manufacturing a channel whose sign is fixed by construction, and it has no exclusion-restriction / instrument-validity analysis and no per-item margin-stratified budget allocation.

Weaver / Shrinking the Generation-Verification Gap with Weak Verifiers: Directly attacks claim (ii): 'estimate signed verifier reliability label-free, then use it to reweight answer selection' is the entire premise of Weaver. Its verifier-filtering step is a de facto polarity/better-than-random screen. Accuracies are estimated per-dataset (shared across items), so its per-item estimation cost is already amortized — undercutting the framing (not the arithmetic) of claim (iii). ISC's remaining differentiation is that Weaver estimates the reliability of the VERIFIERS, whereas ISC uses the verifier as an anchor to identify the sign of the BASE model's self-reported confidence channel, and that Weaver has no identification theory at all.

Training Complex Models with Multi-Task Weak Supervision (MeTaL) + Snorkel / data programming / FlyingSquid: This is the mathematical content of ISC Theorems 1 and 2, already textbook in weak supervision. Theorem 1 ('unanchored channels all flip together, no matter how many') = the known global sign/label-switching ambiguity of conditionally independent latent-class models. Theorem 2 ('one channel with sign known by construction identifies everything') = the known fact that fixing the sign of a single conditionally independent source fixes all the others. ISC gains no credit for the theorems themselves; at most for stating them inside its particular symmetric-confidence-channel parameterization.

Ranking and combining multiple predictors without labeled data (Spectral Meta-Learner) / Estimating the accuracies of multiple classifiers without labeled data: The 12-year-old ancestor of ISC's whole 'estimate signed channel reliability without labels' program, including the sign ambiguity and its resolution by a better-than-random assumption. Anyone reviewing ISC in a stats venue will cite this first and ask why an 'instrument' is needed when a sign convention has sufficed since 2014. ISC's honest answer must be: because in the artifact-echo regime the better-than-random assumption is exactly what fails — that argument, not the theorems, is the contribution.

Hui & Walter two-population design for diagnostic accuracy without a gold standard: Two hits. First, it is the canonical prior instance of 'design creates identification without labels' — 46 years old. Second, and more damaging, it FALSIFIES ISC Theorem 1 as stated: a Hui-Walter-style design identifies the model without any sign-anchored channel, using heterogeneity in prevalence across designed strata instead. So an anchor is one of several known symmetry breakers, not a necessity. ISC's 'necessity' claim is only true inside its own symmetric single-parameter model with a single homogeneous population; it must be restated with those qualifiers or it is simply wrong.

Anchor-based identification: anchor words, anchor points, and the 'good-enough annotator' condition: The word 'anchor', the concept of an anchor, and the theorem shape 'anchor => identification of an otherwise-unidentified latent-class model' are all long-standing terms of art. ISC's 'anchored instrument channel' is an anchor point/anchor annotator relocated to inference time. Reviewers in this area will read Theorems 1-2 as a re-derivation, and Liu et al. 2023's catalogue is a direct rebuttal to the necessity framing.

Instrumental-variable and repeated-measurement identification of nonclassical measurement error / misclassification: This is ISC's Theorem 2 in its econometric home: an extra measurement with a known-sign normalization identifies a latent binary variable plus its misclassification rates. If ISC wants IV language, this is the literature it is joining, and its 'sign known by construction, magnitude unknown' condition is a standard normalization there, not a new idea. Note the terminology risk: ISC calls the verification query an 'instrument' but it is a second MEASUREMENT of the latent truth, not an instrument in the exclusion-restriction sense (it has no treatment to shift). A referee in econometrics will flag the misuse.

Prediction-powered inference and design-based supervised learning with LLM surrogates: This is claim (iii). A fixed calibration/identification cost spread over an arbitrarily large corpus giving O(1/Q) per-item tax is the defining arithmetic of PPI/DSL and is not a result — it is what 'fixed cost' means. ISC's amortization corollary as written ('O(1/SE^2) instrumented items, independent of Q, therefore asymptotically free') will read as a restatement. The only non-obvious part is that ISC's calibration set costs traces rather than human labels and therefore competes with votes for the SAME budget — that trade-off, not the vanishing tax, is the publishable object.

Active WeaSuL: Improving Weak Supervision with Active Learning: This is ISC Phase A's architecture — spend a small, targeted budget on the items where the corpus-level pseudo-label is least trustworthy, and let the corpus-shared parameters improve everywhere — with human labels in place of instrument queries. ISC's 'lowest dedup-weighted margin first' selection rule is a margin-based special case of maxKL sampling. Claim (iii)'s allocation story is therefore prior art in structure; only the substitution of an instrument query for a human label is new.

TEE: Hidden Measurement Error in LLM Pipelines Distorts Annotation, Evaluation, and Benchmarking: Treats prompt design as a first-class design variable competing for a fixed budget against items and replications, at matched cost — the same framing move as ISC section 8, published three months ago. It has no identification/anchor/instrument theory, so it does not touch Theorems 1-2, but it does pre-empt 'the sampling protocol itself is a design variable' as a headline framing.

LLMs as Instruments for Latent Cognitive Variables in Labor Economics: The only paper found that both (a) uses IV/exclusion-restriction language for LLM outputs and (b) enforces the exclusion restriction through deliberate prompt WORDING. That is a genuine precedent for 'design the prompt so the exclusion restriction holds by construction'. It is however an instrument for a treatment in a downstream economic regression, not an anchor for the sign of a latent correctness channel, and it is not at inference time in a test-time-scaling sense. ISC's claim (i) survives only in the narrow form 'instrument for latent CORRECTNESS, constructed per item at inference time'.

Identifiability of parameters in latent structure models with many observed variables: The 'up to label swapping' caveat IS ISC's two-world ambiguity, in full generality and with more channels than ISC's Theorem 1 contemplates. It also shows the correct statement of Theorem 1: with three conditionally independent views everything except the global class labelling is identified, so ISC's instrument is doing exactly one bit of work — resolving a global permutation — which is a much smaller claim than 'converts provably impossible to solvable'.

Gold/honeypot questions in crowdsourcing and Dawid-Skene with gold data: 'Insert a specially designed query whose answer-correctness relation is known in advance, in order to identify a rater's reliability parameter' is 16-year-old crowdsourcing practice. ISC's difference is real but narrow: its inserted query has a known SIGN rather than a known ANSWER, so it needs no labels. That distinction is the cleanest one-sentence novelty statement available and should be foregrounded.

Budget-aware Test-time Scaling via Discriminative Verification: Pre-empts the 'matched total budget, votes vs verifier calls' experimental protocol of ISC section 8 / F1 as a novel methodological contribution. It does not run the artifact-echo cell where extra votes actively hurt, which is where ISC's F1 still has room.

novelty.area: Active/adaptive inference-time compute allocation for LLMs: adaptive sampling, when-to-think/route-to-verifier policies, bandit-based prompt selection, sequential experimental design for LLM querying, information-gain-based query selection
novelty.verdict: From the adaptive-compute-allocation vantage: the generic moves ISC builds on are all published, but the three specific §7 claims survive in this area, with one serious caveat each. CLAIM (i) — IV framing with necessity/sufficiency theorems: OPEN in this literature. Query selection framed as experimental design exists (BED-LLM arXiv:2508.21184; Adaptive Elicitation arXiv:2504.04204 — EIG about a latent), and budgeted BAI for prompts exists (TRIPLE arXiv:2402.09723), but none formulates prompt/query design as instrumental identification of a sign-ambiguous parameter, and none has an impossibility-plus-one-anchor-suffices theorem pair. Caveat: Theorem 1 is a mild extension of TACT's own Prop 7, and the crowdsourcing literature (Karger-Oh-Shah, Oper. Res. 2014; Dawid-Skene descendants) has long known the equivalent gauge ambiguity and resolved it by a better-than-random assumption — ISC must present Theorems 1-2 as replacing that assumption with a constructed anchor, or reviewers from that community will call it known-modulo-restatement. CLAIM (ii) — instrument-identified signed channel reliability, label-free: NOT published in this area. Every verifier-using allocation method found (When-to-Solve-When-to-Verify arXiv:2504.01005; AVA OpenReview:JMDCMf7mlF; GenRM line; SETS; Manvi arXiv:2410.02725) uses verification to rescore/filter the queried item, never to identify a pooled confidence-channel coupling. Nearest miss is Karger-Oh-Shah where allocation queries do double duty (decide items + estimate shared reliabilities, label-free, amortized) — but reliabilities there are of the answer channels themselves with sign fixed by assumption, not identified via a separate anchored instrument. Claim (ii) narrows to: 'first to use anchored side-queries to identify the sign of an unanchored channel' — defensible but must cite crowdsourcing. CLAIM (iii) — vanishing amortized identification tax: the WEAKEST claim as a contribution. The mechanism (a corpus-shared parameter needs O(1/SE^2) probes regardless of Q, so per-item cost → 0) is textbook pooling; amortization of allocation machinery across items is already standard practice in this literature (Damani arXiv:2410.04707 and arXiv:2604.14853 amortize learned allocation policies; Karger-Oh-Shah prove budget-optimal amortized reliability inference; hierarchical/meta-bandits amortize exploration generically). No one has stated the specific 'identification tax vs. per-item rescoring tax' contrast for LLM verification — the CONTRAST is citable as an observation, but do not present the amortization result as a theorem of independent interest. Finally, the direct answer to my assigned question: allocation between 'more solution samples' and 'verification queries' at fixed budget IS published (Singhi et al. static ratio; AVA dynamic VOI) — ISC cannot claim that axis — but NO paper found couples that allocation to a shared-parameter/identification objective; §5's shared-parameter bandit remains open, and F1's 'extra votes amplify an echo, instruments are the only useful budget' argument appears novel and is the strongest differentiator against the entire allocation literature.
closest: When To Solve, When To Verify (Singhi et al., ICML 2025): Directly occupies ISC's 'votes vs. instrument queries at matched total trace budget' axis (spec §5, §8, F1's matched-budget comparison). But the ratio is static/corpus-level, verifications rescore individual solutions (pay-per-item), and there is no identification objective, no shared parameter, no label-free reliability estimation, no theorems about sign identification. Kills any claim that sample-vs-verify budget allocation per se is new; does not touch claims (i)-(iii).

Anytime Verified Agents: Adaptive Compute Allocation for Reliable LLM Reasoning under Budget Constraints: Closest published system to ISC §5's adaptive policy: it literally chooses between 'more samples' and 'verification queries' per state via VOI. However the verifications are used to filter/rescore the current item only; nothing updates a shared cross-item parameter, and there is no identification framing or impossibility theorem. ISC's §5 bandit is 'AVA + a shared-parameter twist', so §5 alone is incremental; the twist (instrument queries identify a pooled coupling) remains unclaimed.

Learning How Hard to Think: Input-Adaptive Allocation of LM Computation (Damani et al., ICLR 2025): Prior art for amortizing an allocation rule across a corpus (train once, apply per item at ~zero marginal cost). But what is amortized is the allocation policy learned from labeled/oracle reward data — not label-free identification of a confidence channel's signed reliability. Weakens the rhetorical force of claim (iii) ('amortization across items is a known move in this literature') without matching its object.

Adaptive-Consistency (Aggarwal et al., EMNLP 2023) and Early-Stopping Self-Consistency (Li et al., ICLR 2024): Establishes that the SC sampling protocol as a per-item and cross-item decision variable is thoroughly mined territory — but only for the 'more base samples or stop' action. None adds a second query type, none can escape TACT-Prop-7-style two-world ambiguity (they all consume the same unanchored channel), none estimates a signed reliability. Bounds ISC's framing novelty ('treats the sampling protocol as a design variable' is not itself new) but leaves (i)-(iii) intact.

TRIPLE: Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification (Shi et al., 2024): The canonical 'bandit-based prompt selection under budget' paper. Reward = observed evaluation scores (needs a scored validation signal); arms are prompts, not answer-candidate instruments; no shared latent across items, no identification-of-sign objective. Related in machinery (budgeted BAI, like ISC's top-2 Mann-Whitney contest) but not in objective.

BED-LLM and Adaptive Elicitation of Latent Information (2025): The nearest 'design of queries for inference about a latent' framing in the LLM literature. But the latent is the per-task target itself, EIG is heuristic (no identifiability impossibility/sufficiency theorems), queries are not sign-anchored instruments, and there is no shared corpus-level parameter whose identification cost amortizes. Claim (i)'s specific content — necessity of an anchored channel, sufficiency of one — has no analogue here.

Strategic Scaling of Test-Time Compute: A Bandit Learning Approach (Zuo et al., 2025): Proves the general point that theoretically-grounded adaptive allocation across items beats uniform — the shell of ISC §5. Allocation is over solution samples only; queries treated independently; no verification arm, no shared-parameter posterior, no identification objective.

Budget-Optimal Task Allocation for Reliable Crowdsourcing Systems (Karger, Oh, Shah, Operations Research 2014): The strongest structural precedent in my area for claims (ii)+(iii) combined: budgeted query allocation where the same queries simultaneously decide items and identify shared reliability parameters, label-free, with the reliability-estimation cost amortized across tasks. Critically, the sign/gauge ambiguity (ISC Theorem 1's two-world swap) is resolved there by ASSUMPTION (workers better than random on average), not by a channel whose sign is fixed by construction — exactly the gap ISC's anchored instrument fills. Any novelty statement must cite this line and position Theorem 1/2 as replacing that assumption with a constructed anchor.

Compute-optimal test-time scaling and mid-generation self-evaluation (Snell et al. 2024; Manvi et al. 2024): Canonical prior art that per-item adaptive allocation policies over the sampling protocol are standard; Manvi's self-evaluation queries are budget spent on judging candidates — but they are unanchored (they are the base channel again, in ISC's terms) and used to rescore, not to identify. No effect on (i)-(iii).

Heteroskedastic Signals in Budgeted LLM Verification (Yang, 2026): Verification-query budget allocation across items with theory — but feedback is ground-truth on verified items (not a noisy sign-anchored instrument), the estimated objects are threshold policies not channel couplings, and no label-free identification. (Note: an initial WebFetch summary of this paper falsely claimed IV-style identification; I verified against the PDF — it contains none. Do not cite it as an IV precedent.)

redteam_issues: [critical] Amortization claim (SPEC-ISC section 4) is false for the estimator as designed and implemented. Phase B (isc.py:155-168) pools D over ALL items, keeping plurality pseudo-labels on the un-instrumented fraction, so effective poisoning is (1-f)*rho_vote + f*epsilon — NOT 'driven by the instrument's error, not the vote's' as the spec claims. Empirically, on a paraphrased-echo cell where plurality labels are 72% wrong, a PERFECT instrument (epsilon=0) at instrument_fraction=0.25 yields d_anchored=+0.187, z=+3.4 — a statistically significant WRONG-signed channel estimate, gamma=+0.17 amplifying the echo, with no diagnostic firing; fraction 0.5 gives z~0; only fraction 1.0 recovers the true sign (-0.371). At fixed m_instr with Q growing, D-hat converges confidently to the plurality-poisoned value: identification does not amortize. The amortization test (test_isc.py:176-190) only checks a benign kappa=0.5 cell where plurality labels are already clean, so it cannot catch this. || FIX: Either compute the pooled D exclusively on instrument-DECIDED items (then amortization is honest but SE is floored by m_instr, and the selection bias of lowest-margin-first must be stated), or retract the O(n_V*m_instr/Q)->0 claim and state that sign identification under a poisoned vote requires instrumenting a constant fraction. Add an amortization test on a dedup-blind echo cell (set dup=I) with fixed m_instr and growing Q, asserting the D sign survives.

[critical] The epsilon sensitivity analysis is not honest about same-model verifiers, and the diagnostics provably cannot detect the realistic failure. The Corollary's delta*(1-2*epsilon) attenuation assumes instrument failure INDEPENDENT of item echo status — the exact class-conditional-noise assumption whose failure created Prop 7 one level down. make_sim_verifier (isc.py:205-230) hardwires item-uniform failure and tests exercise only epsilon in {0,1}. With an echo-CORRELATED verifier (valid on clean items, endorses the belief on echoed items — documented self-preference behavior of same-model verifiers), 41/44 anchored overrides are wrong, I1 and I3 stay silent, and I2 is computed but never gates (isc.py:141-144 vs the gate at :182). F3 'honest failure' is only ever tested against the strawman uniform epsilon_sys=1.0. Additionally epsilon is not estimable label-free (the spec's own section 9(c) requires labels), so the label-free identification guarantee rests on a labeled quantity — this is the two-world unidentifiability reappearing at the instrument level, and the spec never says so. || FIX: State in the Corollary that the relevant epsilon is conditional on the instrumented (low-margin/echo) subset, that echo-correlated verifier error defeats I1-I3 by construction (correlated failure is observationally identical to 'benign corpus + valid instrument'), and that epsilon<1/2 is an untestable assumption, not a checkable condition. Add an epsilon_sys mode correlated with echo status to the simulator, add an F3 variant with it, and either make I2 gate or delete the spec text claiming I2/I3 disambiguate poisoned vote from broken instrument.

[critical] The F1 headline cell is not Prop-7-hard: in the echo sim, echo traces form dup=1.0 cliques, so Phase B's fallback label (dedup-weighted plurality) is already 89% correct (vs raw SC 26%). The D measurement in the F1 test is rescued by dedup, not by the instrument; the ISC win there comes from bypassing TACT-LF's alarms plus per-item overrides. On the genuinely hard cell (paraphrased echo, no lexical signature), ISC at spec defaults scores 0.31-0.47 vs 0.87 at full instrumentation. F1's claim that this is 'the cell where instruments are provably the only use of budget that helps' is unsupported — the cell where that is true is one the tests never construct. || FIX: Add the dedup-blind (paraphrased/systematic-belief) echo cell as the real F1: same confident-wrong majority with dup=identity, where the dedup-weighted plurality is majority-wrong. Report ISC there at the default instrument_fraction, and revise the F1 text to acknowledge that verbatim echo is already handled by dedup.

[major] The world-decision's actual type-I error is ~2x its declared level, and the Mann-Whitney machinery is the wrong tool at these sizes. instrument_item runs TWO uncorrected one-sided tests at alpha_v=0.10 each (isc.py:68-78), and with binary endorsement scores at n_each=3-4 scipy silently uses the asymptotic method (exact is unavailable with ties), ignoring the coarse discrete null. Measured P(decide a world | pure-noise instrument) = 0.217 (n_each=3), 0.167 (n=4), 0.213 (n=8) at nominal 0.10 — inflated and non-monotone in n. F4's claim that the anchored test 'decides the world at its declared error rate' is false as implemented, and test_theorem2_error_control ratifies the inflation by asserting wrong-rate <= 0.15 at alpha=0.05. Theorem 2's 'exponentially decaying error' also silently conflates error with the non-vanishing undecided rate at fixed alpha. || FIX: Replace the double one-sided MW on binary scores with a single exact 2x2 test (Fisher or Boschloo) on endorsement counts, with the winner given by the observed direction, at level alpha_v (or Bonferroni-correct the two one-sided tests). State in Theorem 2 that the exponential rate applies to the wrong-decision probability at fixed alpha while the undecided probability vanishes only as n_V grows. Tighten F4's test to assert the empirical false-decision rate under a null instrument is <= the declared level.

[major] Theorem 1's symmetric-model assumption is doing hidden work, and the theorem statement is incomplete. The swap invariance requires (a) each channel's conditional law symmetric under (y,kappa)->(1-y,-kappa) — a mirror-image location-shift family that real confidence distributions do not satisfy (asymmetric shapes/variances between correct and incorrect break the invariance and can permit unanchored identification from higher moments) — and (b) conditional independence across channels given y, which appears only in the proof sketch, not the theorem statement. The prose conclusion 'Identification requires at least one channel whose sign cannot flip' is a universal claim; what is proved is a minimax impossibility within one symmetric model class. The corresponding test (test_theorem1) is circular — twins share observables by construction, as its own docstring admits — so nothing pins the multi-channel claim; F4's promised 'unanchored multi-channel variant provably cannot' test does not exist. || FIX: Restate Theorem 1 with the conditional-independence assumption explicit and scope the conclusion to the symmetric model class ('no method is uniformly valid over...'). Add the missing F4 multi-channel test: M unanchored symmetric channels on twin pools, asserting empirical world-decision accuracy ~ chance.

[major] The two-candidate restriction is unacknowledged where it bites, and Theorem 2 overclaims what becomes identified. The estimator decides only between the top-2 dedup-weighted candidates (isc.py:59-65); when the correct answer is third-place or absent from the pool, the 'anchored answer' is wrong with certainty and the whole item's pseudo-labels are poisoned — a third world covered by neither Theorem 2 (which conditions on a* in {A,B}) nor the epsilon Corollary. Section 4 says 'top-2 candidates' with no caveat. Further, 'the base channel's per-item sign, and TACT's pooled D, become identified' overclaims: per-item sign at fixed m traces is never identified (SE per item ~0.15 even at m=40 per SPEC-TACT 4.7); what is estimated is a pooled D on the lowest-margin-selected slice — a biased estimand under heterogeneous kappa_q, since low-margin items are precisely where the channel plausibly decouples (TACT's own E2 premise), and SE_jack does not correct selection bias. || FIX: Add to Theorem 2 and section 4 the explicit conditioning a* in {top-2} and treat P(a* not in top-2) as an additional additive error term alongside epsilon. Replace 'per-item sign becomes identified' with 'the pooled D over instrument-decided items becomes identified up to instrument validity', and state the selection-bias caveat for the lowest-margin-first rule under heterogeneous kappa.

[minor] Index-misalignment bug: estimate_isc builds dis_idx/agr_idx with zip(chosen, results) (isc.py:148-149), but results omits items where instrument_item returned None while chosen does not — whenever any chosen item is single-answer, every subsequent item's margin is attributed to the wrong pool, corrupting the I3 diagnostic. || FIX: Track (idx, result) pairs together, e.g. append (int(idx), res) in the Phase A loop and build dis_idx/agr_idx from that list.

[critical] The simulated verifier is an error-free oracle at every setting used, so the headline measures the oracle, not the estimator. On the 400-item headline corpus with make_sim_verifier(p_v=0.85): decided-correct = 1.0000 at n_v=4 (204/399 decided), 1.0000 at n_v=8 (298/399), 1.0000 at n_v=16 (385/399) — zero wrong decisions in ~890 decided items. The correct answer is in the dedup-weighted top-2 on 99.75% of items, so instrument_item is always asked a binary question containing the truth. make_sim_verifier (/Users/vito/development/adaptive-reasoning-consensus/src/rlev_voi/isc.py lines 205-230) draws i.i.d. Bernoulli(p_v) per query keyed on pool.correct, with no correlation to item difficulty, to the base channel, or across queries. The only correlated-failure knob, epsilon_sys, is all-or-nothing per item and its failure mode is 'endorse the plurality', which degrades to SC and can never point at a third wrong answer. The simulator cannot produce a harmful instrument, so the conclusion is assumed. || FIX: Add a difficulty-coupled verifier (p_v_item = sigmoid(a + b*item_difficulty), so verifier and solver fail on the same items) and make that correlation the swept axis instead of a Bernoulli mixture. Add an adversarial mode where the invalid verifier endorses a wrong NON-plurality candidate, so failure can cost more than falling back to SC. Report decided-correct rate as a first-class field in ISCEstimate.diagnostics and print it in every table — a row reading 1.000 is a row about an oracle.

Separately the Corollary's ε<1/2 breakdown point is unguarded: at epsilon_sys=0.6 and 0.8 ISC still ships gamma=-0.643 and -0.453 with no alarm firing. test_F3_systematic_belief_echo_triggers_fallback (/Users/vito/development/adaptive-reasoning-consensus/tests/test_isc.py lines 159-172) probes only epsilon_sys=1.0, the one point where I3 fires. || FIX: Add the non-echo wrong-majority cell and an epsilon_sys sweep {0.3,0.5,0.6,0.8} to tests/test_isc.py asserting acc >= SC - 0.02 in every cell, and let them fail until the guard is real. Gate on it — require the anchored-subset D and the plurality-subset D to agree in sign before shipping a nonzero gamma, else fall back. That also gives I1-I3 a test that distinguishes 'instrument works' from 'instrument outvoted'.

[major] The Mann-Whitney test does not run at its declared level, so Theorem 2's error control and F4 are unsupported. instrument_item (/Users/vito/development/adaptive-reasoning-consensus/src/rlev_voi/isc.py lines 67-79) runs BOTH one-sided tests, each at alpha_v, making the effective level 2*alpha_v while SPEC-ISC §4 calls it 'the one-sided test at level alpha_V'. Worse, scipy's default method='auto' falls back to the normal approximation on heavily tied binary scores: at 2 observations per side it returns p=0.0970 where the exact minimum attainable p-value is 0.1667 — an impossible value that lets n_v=4 decide 204/399 items. Measured empirical type-I with a signal-free verifier (p_v=0.5, alpha_v=0.10): 0.138 (n_v=4), 0.213 (n_v=6), 0.168 (n_v=8), 0.206 (n_v=16), 0.148 (n_v=40) — 1.4-2.1x the declared level and not decreasing in n_v. n_v<6 is also silently undecidable under an exact test, which contradicts the 'vanishing per-item tax' story that needs small n_v. || FIX: Pass method='exact' (or use a Fisher/binomial test, which is what Bernoulli endorsement scores call for) and split the level — alpha_v/2 per side, or one two-sided test with the direction read off the sign of r. Add a guard rejecting n_v below the smallest value whose exact minimum p-value <= alpha_v (n_v>=6 at alpha_v=0.10). Then implement F4 as pre-registered: a null-instrument type-I experiment asserting empirical decision rate <= alpha_v. Note test_theorem1_unanchored_channels_cannot_distinguish_twins (tests/test_isc.py lines 45-57) is a tautology on identical arrays, not the 'empirical type-I ~ chance for an unanchored multi-channel variant' that SPEC-ISC lines 140-142 promise.

[major] The headline and ablation results are unreproducible from the repo. results/isc_echo_headline.json and results/isc_channel_ablation.json were committed (06993b9, 8d60f27) with no generating script — nothing under /Users/vito/development/adaptive-reasoning-consensus/experiments/ references estimate_isc, isc_vote or make_sim_verifier. The ablation table also stops at frac=0.5, omitting frac=1.0 — the cell where verify-only is strongest (0.7075 at T=4.0, a 0.15 gap rather than the 0.32 the commit message advertises). || FIX: Commit experiments/run_isc_eval.py that regenerates both JSONs, writing n_items, data seed, estimator seed, p_v, alpha_v and n_v into the output. Report mean +/- s.e. over >=10 seeds rather than one, and extend the ablation to frac=1.0. The seed spread is only ~0.02 so the conclusion does not move, but the selection has to be visible.

[major] Results depend on PYTHONHASHSEED, so runs are not reproducible across processes. make_sim_verifier (/Users/vito/development/adaptive-reasoning-consensus/src/rlev_voi/isc.py line 221) seeds the item-level validity draw with abs(hash((pool.meta.get('qid', id(pool)), 'sys'))) % 2**32. hash() of a tuple containing a str is randomized per interpreter, and when meta has no 'qid' the fallback is id(pool), a memory address. Measured on the headline corpus at epsilon_sys=0.5 with stable string qids: gamma = -0.7308 / -0.7478 / -0.7490 and accuracy 0.6675 / 0.6775 / 0.6775 under PYTHONHASHSEED = 0 / 1 / 2; with the id(pool) fallback the spread widens to 0.6450-0.7025. Every epsilon_sys number in this review and in the repo is process-dependent. || FIX: Replace hash() with a stable digest — int.from_bytes(hashlib.blake2b(str(qid).encode(), digest_size=8).digest(), 'big') — and make qid mandatory, raising rather than falling back to id(pool). generate_item in /Users/vito/development/adaptive-reasoning-consensus/src/rlev_voi/simulate.py should stamp a deterministic meta['qid'] on every pool.

[major] No matched-budget comparison against a more-diverse-sampling arm exists anywhere. The only rival use of budget tested is K=12 vs K=20 from the identical SimConfig (tests/test_isc.py lines 127-133), where echo_prob is a fixed DGP parameter — so 'extra plain votes do not help' is a property of the generator, not a finding. I swept the obvious rival (decoding/prompt diversification, modelled as lowering echo_prob at constant K=12): SC goes 0.2950 → 0.3025 → 0.3100 → 0.3425 → 0.3400 as echo_prob falls 0.85 → 0. That leaves ISC's case intact in this cell, but only because the wrong cluster's 0.60 weight — not its echo rate — is what defeats SC. Nothing in the repo establishes this, and 'big <= small + 0.02' is not a test of the diversity alternative. || FIX: Add a diversity arm to the headline table: at matched total traces, ISC vs SC-with-diversified-sampling (echo_prob or cluster-weight perturbation as the knob) vs dedup-SC. State in SPEC-ISC §6/F1 that the wrong-cluster mass, not the echo rate, is what plain votes cannot fix — that is both the real reason an instrument is needed and a stronger claim than the current one.

[minor] The F2 and amortization tests are too weak to detect the failure modes above. test_F2_benign_negative_channel_isc_matches_tact_lf and test_amortization_channel_estimate_stabilizes_with_fixed_instrumented_count (/Users/vito/development/adaptive-reasoning-consensus/tests/test_isc.py lines 137-190) each run a single seed with loose thresholds (isc_acc >= lf_acc - 0.02; d_anchored > 0.2), and the amortization test checks only the SIGN of d at two corpus sizes — never the standard error, which is the quantity the O(1/SE^2) claim in SPEC-ISC §4 is about. A method whose gamma flips sign across budget (see the F3 issue) passes both. || FIX: Seed-sweep both tests (>=10 seeds, assert on the mean and the worst case) and rewrite the amortization test to assert pooled.se at fixed instrumented count is within tolerance across corpus sizes, not merely that d_hat keeps its sign.
redteam_verdicts: Reject in current form; the core symmetry-breaking idea is sound but all three headline claims fail under adversarial scrutiny. Theorem 1 is a minimax statement inside a symmetric, conditionally-independent model class presented as universal necessity (the symmetric-model assumption is doing the work — asymmetric real confidence laws can be identified without an anchor). Theorem 2 is directionally right but its estimator decides only top-2 worlds (the a*-not-in-top-2 third world is unhandled), its 'declared error rate' is empirically ~2x nominal (double one-sided asymptotic Mann-Whitney on n=3 binary tied scores; measured 0.17-0.22 false-decision rate under a null instrument at alpha=0.10), and 'per-item sign identified' overclaims a selection-biased pooled estimate. The exclusion restriction is the method's load-bearing wall and the epsilon analysis is a strawman for the same-model verifier it names: failure is modeled as item-uniform, tested only at epsilon in {0,1}, while an echo-correlated verifier (the realistic self-preference mode) produces 41/44 wrong anchored overrides with zero diagnostics firing — the two-world unidentifiability reappears at the instrument level and the spec does not say so. Worst, the amortization claim is contradicted by the implementation's own Phase B: with a PERFECT instrument at fraction 0.25 on a dedup-blind echo cell, the pooled D is significantly wrong-signed (z=+3.4) and gamma amplifies the echo, because plurality labels on the un-instrumented 75% dominate the pool — identification requires a constant instrumented fraction, so the 'vanishing identification tax' (novelty claim iii) is hollow. The F1 headline cell is not even Prop-7-hard: dedup already fixes 89% of its pseudo-labels. Salvageable via: pooled D on decided items only, exact 2x2 world test, correlated-epsilon failure mode in sim + F3, dedup-blind hard cell as F1, and rescoped theorem statements.

Not validated — the headline experiment does not support claims (ii)/(iii), and the one falsifier pre-registered as mandatory (F1) fails against a free baseline that already exists in this repo. I reproduced results/isc_echo_headline.json exactly (echo cell, n=400, data seed=42, K=12, estimate_isc seed=7 — none of which is recorded anywhere; no generating script is committed) and then ran the ablations SPEC-ISC never ran.

(1) THE CIRCULARITY IS REAL AND MEASURABLE. At the headline setting the simulated verifier is not merely "anchored", it is error-free: of the items instrument_item decides, decided-correct = 1.0000 at n_v=4 (204/399 decided), 1.0000 at n_v=8 (298/399), 1.0000 at n_v=16 (385/399). Not one wrong decision in ~890 decided items. A wrong decision requires both queries on the true candidate to fail AND both on the false candidate to endorse, p≈5e-4/item. The correct answer is in the dedup-weighted top-2 on 99.75% of items, so the instrument is always handed a binary question containing the truth. "ISC beats SC" here is arithmetic on an injected oracle.

(2) THE CRITICAL ABLATION YOU NAMED, RUN. I ablated the INSTRUMENT while keeping the channel (estimate_isc Phase B verbatim with anchored={}, i.e. plurality pseudo-labels + same tempering, alarms off): d_hat=-0.546, gamma=-1.051, accuracy 0.6225 — versus the headline 0.675 at 0.4 extra traces/item with gamma=-1.06. ~89% of the gain over the 0.295 floor, and the exponent to two decimals, comes with ZERO instrument queries. The committed "critical ablation" (commit 8d60f27) ablates the channel while keeping the instrument, answering an objection nobody would raise. The live objection is "this is TACT-LF with the E1 alarm switched off", and on the headline cell it stands.

(3) A ZERO-BUDGET BASELINE BEATS FULL ISC. Dedup-weighted plurality — the repo's own baselines.run_dedup_sc, whose core routine tact._dedup_weights is called inside estimate_isc — scores 0.8575 (0.9600 at K=20), and 0.9275 in ISC's own dedup-plurality formulation, at zero extra traces. Full ISC reaches 0.9050 only at 8 extra traces/item (+67% budget). F1's "instruments are provably the only use of budget that helps" is false in the very simulator that produced it. The K=12-vs-K=20 contrast is same-DGP resampling: echo fraction is a fixed parameter, so "more votes don't help" is true by construction. No diversity-inducing baseline is tested at all.

(4) HONEST FAILURE (F3) DOES NOT HOLD OUTSIDE THE TUNED CELL. In a non-echo wrong-majority cell where dedup cannot help (SC=0.3400), ISC at frac=0.1/n_v=8 returns gamma=-0.326 and accuracy 0.1325 — less than half the floor, worse than verify-only (0.3400), with I1 and I3 both silent. Across budget the exponent flips -0.326 → 0.000 → +1.392. The Corollary's ε<1/2 breakdown is unguarded too: at epsilon_sys=0.6/0.8 ISC still ships gamma=-0.643/-0.453 with no alarm; test_F3 probes only epsilon_sys=1.0, the single point where I3 happens to fire.

What survives: at matched total budget the channel does add over verify-only within this simulator (T=4.0/item: verify-only frac=1.0,n_v=4 → 0.7075 vs full ISC frac=0.5,n_v=8 → 0.8575), and Theorem 1's statement is sound. But that margin sits on top of a perfect oracle, is smaller than what a free dedup baseline delivers, and inverts to a large loss one cell over. SPEC-ISC §9 already lists the red team as pending — treat this as it. Do not publish the echo-cell number in any form until items 1-4 are closed.
